hz11_pattern.topic: Threat claims against outcomes: Iran's bomb warnings vs intelligence assessments

claims.text: NIE key judgments read by Hadley 3 Dec 2007: 'The intelligence community has high confidence that Iran halted its covert nuclear weapons program in the fall of 2003' and 'moderate confidence that it had not restarted that program as of mid-2007'; Hadley: 'the risk of Iran acquiring a nuclear weapon remains a very serious problem'

Sept 2012: Netanyahu told the UN General Assembly Iran was about one year away from a weapon; a Mossad report dated October 2012, shared with South Africa and leaked in the Spy Cables (Guardian and Al Jazeera, 23 Feb 2015), said Iran 'is not performing the activity necessary to produce weapons' and 'does not appear to be ready to enrich' to higher levels

Times of Israel (Ginsburg, 24 Feb 2015) argued the memo was not contradictory: the full passage described progress toward a weapon and Netanyahu's claim concerned enough enriched uranium, not a finished weapon; the disagreement was over speed

Gabbard to House Intelligence Committee, 26 March 2025: the intelligence community 'continues to assess that Iran is not building a nuclear weapon' and Khamenei 'has not authorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003'; also said the enriched uranium stockpile is at its highest levels, unprecedented for a state without nuclear weapons

Nov 2024 US intelligence report: Iran 'is not building a nuclear weapon' but has 'undertaken activities that better position it to produce one, if it so chooses'; Gen. Kurilla testified Iran could produce enough material for 10 weapons in three weeks; Sen. Warner: nothing in recent intelligence contradicted Gabbard
June 2025: Trump said 'I don't care what she said' and that Iran was 'very close' to a bomb; Netanyahu described a nuclear-armed Iran as an imminent threat; Iran says its programme is peaceful

hz11_proxies.topic: Groups Israel itself armed or funded: Syrian rebels 2013-18, Gaza militias 2025-26

claims.text: Foreign Policy (6 Sep 2018), based on interviews with more than two dozen commanders and fighters: Israel secretly armed and funded at least 12 rebel groups in southern Syria from 2013, expanded 2014, ended July 2018; about $75 a month per fighter plus money for black-market weapons; assault rifles, machine guns, mortar launchers, vehicles; early shipments US-made M16s, later arms from a 2009 Iranian shipment to Hezbollah that Israel seized; delivered through three gates on the Golan; aim to keep Iran-backed forces and Islamic State away from the border; Israeli embassy in Washington declined to comment; a fighter: 'This is a lesson we will not forget about Israel'
Eisenkot told the Sunday Times (Jan 2019) Israel supplied light arms to Syrian rebels 'for self-defense'; Israel had previously acknowledged only humanitarian aid

5 June 2025: Avigdor Lieberman disclosed Israel was arming Gaza clans and said the government was giving weapons to 'a group of criminals and felons identified with Islamic State'; NPR could not substantiate; Israeli media identified a gang led by Yasser Abu Shabab, accused of looting UN aid convoys

Netanyahu, 5 June 2025: 'Liberman leaked that on security officials' advice, we activated clans in Gaza who oppose Hamas. What's wrong with that? It only saves IDF soldiers' lives'; called it 'a criminal leak'

Washington Post obtained an October 2024 internal UN memo saying gangs in Gaza 'may be benefitting from a passive if not active benevolence' or 'protection' from the Israeli army; one gang leader had a 'military-like compound' in an area 'restricted, controlled and patrolled by the IDF'

Abu Shabab killed 4 Dec 2025 in eastern Rafah in a clash with the Abu Suneima family; accounts conflict; group denied Hamas responsibility; deputy Ghassan Duhine took over; the Popular Forces operated in eastern Rafah under Israeli control

ACLED (27 Apr 2026): at least five anti-Hamas armed groups operate from Israel-controlled areas east of the Yellow Line; more than 40 violent events and nearly 80 fatalities since the October 2025 ceasefire; ACLED says Israel provides weapons, logistics, intelligence and training and has used drones during their clashes; groups also abducted and killed civilians accused of collaborating with Hamas; ACLED judges they pose no existential threat to Hamas alone

hz11_fill.topic: Netanyahu's earlier warnings on Iran's nuclear timeline, 1992-2018, against the record

claims.text: In 1992, as a member of the Knesset, Netanyahu said Iran was three to five years from being able to produce a nuclear weapon and that the threat had to be 'uprooted by an international front headed by the U.S.' (reported in retrospectives; the Week traces it to a Christian Science Monitor timeline; no primary Knesset record fetched)

In his 1995 book Fighting Terrorism Netanyahu repeated a short timeline: Mondoweiss quotes p.121 as 'The best estimates at this time place Iran between three and five years away from possessing the prerequisites required'; The Week gives 'five to seven years at most'. Wording not checked against the book itself.

10 July 1996, address to joint session of Congress: Iran 'the most dangerous of these regimes'; if it or Iraq acquired nuclear weapons 'this could presage catastrophic consequences'; 'the deadline for attaining this goal is getting extremely close' (goal = stopping nuclearization of terrorist states, led by the US)

12 September 2002, House Government Reform hearing 'Conflict with Iraq: An Israeli Perspective': Netanyahu said 'Saddam is seeking and is working and is advancing toward the development of nuclear weapons', spoke of 'centrifuges the size of washing machines', said removing Saddam 'will have enormous positive reverberations on the region', and said Iraq and Iran were vying to be first to nuclear weapons while 'I don't know that Iran has nuclear weapons.'

February 2009 US embassy cable (09TELAVIV457, released by WikiLeaks) records Netanyahu telling a congressional delegation Iran was 'probably one or two years away' (reported by The Intercept, The Week, Al Jazeera)
27 September 2012 UNGA: Netanyahu called for a 'clear red line' on Iran's enrichment, saying Iran could complete the second stage 'by next summer at the latest'

30 April 2018 Netanyahu presented documents from Iran's 'Project Amad' (about 55,000 pages and 183 CDs) saying Iran had lied; the documents appeared to date to the early 2000s, and he showed no direct evidence Iran had violated the 2015 deal; Iran denied ever seeking nuclear weapons; Zarif called him 'the boy who can't stop crying wolf'
Duelfer report (Iraq Survey Group), 6 October 2004: Saddam 'ended Iraq's nuclear program after the 1991 Gulf War' and 'did not possess stockpiles of illicit weapons at the time of the U.S. invasion'
